content.user_title: Polish Web App UI and UX
content.value_statement: Many working web apps still feel uneven on desktop and mobile. This skill gives agents an iterative polishing workflow for sharper layouts, states, and responsive details.
actual_capabilities: Provides a reusable prompt for iterative UI and UX polish passes.
Directs separate review of desktop and mobile experiences.
Lists visual, interaction, mobile, and desktop areas to improve.
Explains when to use polishing instead of a full redesign.
Shows optional Beads task examples for organizing UI polish work.
limitations: It assumes the application already works and has basic styling.
It does not provide a complete design system from scratch.
It requires human review to catch regressions after each pass.
The Beads workflow examples require a separate local tool.

use_cases.title: Refine a launch-ready product
use_cases.description: Improve spacing, typography, states, and responsive behavior before a release.

use_cases.title: Guide design QA passes
use_cases.description: Use repeated agent reviews to find small visual and interaction issues across screens.

use_cases.title: Organize multi-agent polish work
use_cases.description: Split desktop and mobile polish tasks so several agents can improve different areas.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Polish Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one focused improvement pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this working web app and improve the UI and UX polish. Focus on spacing, typography, visual hierarchy, states, and responsive behavior. Keep changes incremental and avoid changing core functionality.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Desktop and Mobile
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for separate modality review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Polish the app with separate attention to desktop and mobile. For desktop, improve layout density, hover states, and keyboard-friendly flows. For mobile, improve touch targets, spacing, navigation, and breakpoint behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Repeat Until Improvements Shrink
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured iteration for an app that is already stable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run another UI and UX polish pass on this app. Look for small remaining issues in visual consistency, accessibility, interaction feedback, and responsive details. Stop when changes become minor or risky.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Polish Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for dividing work across screens or agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a focused polish plan for this app. Separate desktop and mobile tasks by screen, assign clear areas of ownership, and list the checks needed after each pass to prevent regressions.

output_examples.input: A dashboard works, but the spacing, button states, and mobile layout feel unfinished.
output_examples.output: The skill guides an agent to tighten spacing, improve hierarchy, add clearer feedback states, and test the dashboard separately on desktop and mobile.

output_examples.input: A team wants several agents to polish different pages before launch.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests splitting polish work by page and modality, then reviewing each pass for visual consistency, accessibility, and regressions.

best_practices: Fix functional bugs before using the polish workflow.
Review each iteration before asking for another pass.
Test changes on real desktop and mobile viewports.
anti_patterns: Using polish prompts to replace a missing design system.
Running many passes without reviewing the changes.
Optimizing visuals while ignoring accessibility and performance.

faq.question: What kind of projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits working web apps that already have basic styling and need refinement before release.

faq.question: Does it create a full redesign?
faq.answer: No. It is for incremental polish, not full information architecture or design system work.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it separate desktop and mobile?
faq.answer: Desktop and mobile have different layout, interaction, and navigation needs. Separate review reduces weak compromises.

faq.question: How many passes should I run?
faq.answer: Run a pass, review it, and repeat while changes remain useful and low risk.

faq.question: Does it require Beads?
faq.answer: No. Beads examples are optional workflow guidance for teams that already use that tool.
